```{python}
#| label: prepare-dashboard
#| include: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
sales = [120, 135, 128, 160, 175, 190]
total = sum(sales)
growth = (sales[-1] / sales[0] - 1) * 100
```

## Summary {.flow}

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: Total units sold
dict(value=f"{total:,}")
```

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: January to June growth
dict(value=f"{growth:.1f}%")
```

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: Latest month
dict(value=f"{sales[-1]:,} units")
```

## Details

```{python}
#| title: Monthly trend
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.plot(months, sales, marker="o", color="#23745b", linewidth=2)
ax.set(xlabel="Month", ylabel="Units sold")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| title: Underlying values
rows = "\n".join(f"| {month} | {value} |" for month, value in zip(months, sales))
display(Markdown("| Month | Units sold |\n|:------|-----------:|\n" + rows))
```

## Notes {.flow}

::: {.card title="Read this dashboard"}
All values are fictional. Growth compares June with January; the total covers
all six months. KPI cards, the chart, and the table use the same Python data.

Edit the `sales` list and render again to update every view. Level-two headings
define rows, and cells within each row become cards. `scrolling: true` allows
the page to grow with its content. No application server is needed after rendering.
:::
